name: Yangshao culture
title: The story of the Yangshao culture

text: About 7,000 years ago, farmers lived along the middle Yellow River in China.
They grew millet above all, and they kept pigs and dogs.
src: a Neolithic culture that spread widely along the middle reaches of the Yellow River in China between about 5000 and 3000 BCE
The Yangshao people lived mainly on millet / Pigs were the main source of meat and dogs were kept

text: They grew some rice too, and brewed beer from millet and rice for shared feasts.
src: They also grew and ate rice, though less of it / brewing beer and communal feasting were integral to Yangshao culture: the beer was made mainly from common millet and rice

text: A home was a round pit about a metre deep, with walls of woven sticks and mud.
Houses stood around a central square, and some villages were ringed by ditches.
src: A typical home was dug as a rounded pit about a metre deep, walled with woven wattle plastered with mud
Villages typically covered ten to fourteen acres, with houses set round a central square / Some villages were enclosed by ditches

text: Farmers used polished stone axes, hoes and sickles.
Potters, working without a wheel, painted their pots with human faces, fish and patterns.
src: Stone tools were polished and highly specialised. Farmers used axes, hoes, sickles and millstones
Unlike the later Longshan culture, they did not use the potter’s wheel / decorated with human faces, animals and geometric designs / fish patterns were favoured at first

text: They wove cloth from hemp and made a little silk.
src: The Yangshao wove hemp and produced a little silk

text: A dragon figure they made is the oldest known picture of a dragon in the world.
Today the village of Yangshao, which gave the culture its name, has a museum next to its excavations.
src: A dragon figure dating to the fifth millennium BCE is the world’s oldest known depiction of a dragon
Today the Yangshao site in Mianchi County, Sanmenxia, which gave the culture its name, has a museum next to the excavations
